title: FromSoftware
subtitle: the Souls line and its adjacents, in release order
blurb: 10 games — about 337 hours of story, 266 of it the Souls line proper.
notes: The Souls line and what sits beside it, not the whole studio — no King's Field, no older Armored Core, no Déraciné, no Duskbloods. Armored Core VI is the one marked outlier, included because it is what the studio built between Elden Ring and its expansion; skip it and nothing breaks.

HowLongToBeat main-story figures, as asked — the credits, not completion. These are the games where skill moves the number more than anywhere else on this site, so treat every figure as a median, not a promise.
Tiers, and the rule behind them.

1 is the Souls line proper: the seven complete games from Demon's Souls to Elden Ring, about 266 hours. 2 is what extends Elden Ring — Shadow of the Erdtree and Nightreign. 3 is the outlier. A finish date covers 1 and 2; the checkbox adds Armored Core.
Erdtree is a row, on purpose.
Shadow of the Erdtree is DLC, but it is the size of a full game and most of a playthrough long, so it gets its own tracked row rather than a footnote on Elden Ring.
Remaster and remake, noted rather than listed.

Dark Souls: Remastered (2018) and the Demon's Souls remake (2020) are the same stories in better clothes. Play whichever edition you like and tick the one row — separate rows would double-count the same game.
Game list and years from Wikipedia's FromSoftware article; hours from HowLongToBeat, collected from its own pages and verified by name.
